scope: Audited Malcolmson incoming letters 528, 533, 535, 548, 559 and 1147 against dated Darwin outgoing records in all_letters.jsonl.

incoming_reviews.summary: Malcolmson answers Darwin's elevation questions with evidence and quotations about Malacca, Penang, Quedah, Coromandel, Bombay, Arabia, Java and Keeling/Cocos, while identifying publications, specimens and other observers.
incoming_reviews.assessment: Substantive incoming answer, but cited publications and specimens do not establish Darwin receipt or later use. The Keeling reference is too generic to identify a Darwin witness.

evidence.quote: answer your letter
memoir on the Keeling islands
At Shahar on the south coast of Arabia I found recent coral & shells raised considerably

incoming_reviews.summary: Malcolmson explains the delayed reply, distinguishes Darwin's former and last letters, reports Glen Roy discussion and extensive Arabia observations at Sahar, Aden, Kamran and Jedda, and leaves the letter incomplete.
incoming_reviews.assessment: Detailed incoming observations, but no located later Darwin writing repeats a distinctive Sahar, Kamran or Jedda detail or attributes it to Malcolmson.

evidence.quote: the delay has enabled me to get some information that, I hope, will be of use to you
I have not yet received your paper from London
Here then is an island that has been raised at least 40 feet above the highest level of the sea

incoming_reviews.summary: Malcolmson reports Allan's Aldabra and coral views, encloses Hardie's Macclesfield Bank sounding, discusses trout with Shier and Agassiz, and describes grooved sandstone, submarine peat and a difficulty for Darwin's erratic-block theory. He had not received Darwin's paper.
incoming_reviews.assessment: The first of the two letters later identified editorially as a route for Allan's coral information. The body establishes Malcolmson-to-Darwin transmission and Allan's expected reply; the dated Darwin witness below documents only the later Coral reefs presentation route.

evidence.quote: Dr Allan has got your last letter
more of this when he answers your questions in detail
It strikes me as a difficulty to your erratic block theory

incoming_reviews.summary: Malcolmson sends a coralline specimen, explains worm-bored grooves, reports Allan's Aldabra and Comoros views and planned coral-growth experiments, offers Indian specimens, and asks Darwin to forward a packet to Royle.
incoming_reviews.assessment: Direct incoming information and specimen route. The Allan passage is distinctive and is the strongest source for the later Darwin-to-Allan Coral reefs distribution evidence, although Darwin's body does not name Malcolmson as the route.

evidence.quote: send you a specimen of a coralline
Allan promised to write you a long letter
very important experiments on the growth of coral. 3 feet in 6 months

incoming_reviews.summary: Surviving fragment comments on Darwin's Journal of researches pages 619 and 621-2, Agassiz's Jura models and blocks, Malcolmson's Fifeshire grooved sandstone observations, and the limits of glacier theory. Its editorial date is held and rests on assumed Journal receipt.
incoming_reviews.assessment: Evidence of Malcolmson's discussion of Darwin's published text, but date and receipt premise are conditional. No later Darwin outgoing repeats the distinctive Fifeshire evidence or acknowledges the fragment.

evidence.quote: The shores of the Tertiary sea of the Jura
grooved and polished surfaces exactly like the limestone of Neuchatel
can hardly be explained by the theory of glaciers

incoming_reviews.summary: Malcolmson recommends Robertson for Geological Society membership, thanks Darwin for the Glen Roy paper, reports Stables's parallel-road observations and his own drift, raised-beach, terrace and boulder observations, and leaves the letter incomplete.
incoming_reviews.assessment: Proves Malcolmson read Darwin's paper by a few days before 2 January 1840 and discussed it with Stables. It is an incoming acknowledgment, not Darwin voice or proof of a later Darwin receipt. A later Darwin letter has only a generic reference to several private communications.

evidence.quote: I have to thank you for your most interesting paper on Glen Roy, which I read with great interest
single lines almost 60 feet broad
Everywhere along the eastern coast a series of terraces can be traced far above the common line of raised beaches

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin sends Henslow Maldeeve and Chagos specimens, compares them with Keeling Island, encloses a worm-paper abstract and discusses coral and plant-colour questions.
witness_reviews.assessment: No Malcolmson attribution; Darwin's own Indian Ocean material is an independent source for the generic Keeling comparison.

evidence.quote: islands precisely like Keeling Island

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Hall on Coquimbo, Patagonia and Glen Roy terraces and adds a postscript about other Scottish parallel roads and private communications.
witness_reviews.assessment: Generic plural does not identify 1147 in Darwin's body; footnote 9 names Malcolmson only editorially. Candidate lead, not secure knowledge edge.

evidence.quote: I have received several private communications on the subject.
See, for example, Correspondence vol. 1, letter from J. G. Malcolmson, 2 January 1840.

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin sends Agassiz his Journal and discusses boulders and glacier criticism.
witness_reviews.assessment: General boulder/glacier overlap only; no Malcolmson-specific observation or attribution.

evidence.quote: I take the liberty of sending you a copy of my Journal

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin gives Lyell an extended argument about Agassiz, glaciers, floating ice, Jura blocks, Glen Roy and South American boulders.
witness_reviews.assessment: No Malcolmson attribution or distinctive Macclesfield, Fifeshire or Arabian detail.

evidence.quote: Some facts about boulders in Chiloe

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin sends Lonsdale his paper on South American erratic boulders for the Geological Society.
witness_reviews.assessment: No Malcolmson-specific content or attribution; general boulder terminology insufficient.

evidence.quote: I send you the accompanying paper for the disposal of the Society

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin discusses coral-limestone, mangrove swamps, Red Sea and Bermuda reefs using his observations and named authorities.
witness_reviews.assessment: No Allan or Malcolmson attribution and no distinctive Malacca, Coromandel, Aldabra or Comoros detail.

evidence.quote: Moresby

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin's date-held memorandum for Lyell discusses subsidence and coral-reef preservation.
witness_reviews.assessment: General coral theory; date uncertain; no Malcolmson or Allan attribution.

evidence.quote: Considering the probability of subsidence in the middle of the great oceans being very slow

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin gives Smith Elder distribution instructions for Coral reefs, including routing a presentation copy to Dr Allan of Forres.
witness_reviews.assessment: Strongest dated Darwin witness for the Malcolmson-to-Allan provenance route, but body documents book distribution rather than first receipt. Footnote 7 explicitly connects 535 and 548 and is editorial evidence.

evidence.quote: The copy for Dr Allan of Forres in Scotland might be sent to Edinburgh & then forwarded
via John Grant Malcolmson (see Correspondence vol. 2, letters from J. G. Malcolmson, 7 October 1839 and 30 November 1839)

witness_reviews.summary: Copied Darwin excerpt to Fitton about extinct glaciers in North Wales, floating ice and Glen Roy.
witness_reviews.assessment: Darwin-authored surviving prose but no Malcolmson-specific evidence.

evidence.quote: my views, of the distribution of the boulders on the S. american plains, has been effected by floating Ice are correct

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin writes Lyell about coral species, Chagos dead reefs, Moresby, Society politics and the Glen Roy dispute.
witness_reviews.assessment: Named Moresby and Darwin observations are alternate sources; no Malcolmson or Allan attribution.

evidence.quote: after the clear & positive accounts of Capt. Moresby

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin replies to Maclaren's criticism of Coral reefs on fringing reefs, denudation, limestone thickness and subsidence.
witness_reviews.assessment: Response to Maclaren's published criticism; no Allan or Malcolmson attribution.

evidence.quote: Your third objection appears to me much the most, indeed the only, formidable one

witness_reviews.summary: Darwin sends Dieffenbach Coral reefs and papers on the Concepcion earthquake and erratic boulders, with editorial and translation instructions.
witness_reviews.assessment: General coral and boulder references are Darwin's publications; no Malcolmson or Allan attribution.

evidence.quote: I transmit for your acceptance a copy of a small work on Coral-Reefs

dispositions.reason: 548 supplies the distinctive Allan coral route; 629A is dated Darwin instruction to send Coral reefs to Dr Allan. Editorial footnote 7 confirms Malcolmson's 7 October and 30 November letters as the information route. Darwin's body does not name Malcolmson, so provenance is candidate-only.
dispositions.response_scope: DCP-LETT-629A body paragraph 4 only; date documents distribution/knowledge by then, not first receipt.

evidence.quote: Allan promised to write you a long letter
very important experiments on the growth of coral. 3 feet in 6 months
The copy for Dr Allan of Forres in Scotland might be sent to Edinburgh & then forwarded
via John Grant Malcolmson (see Correspondence vol. 2, letters from J. G. Malcolmson, 7 October 1839 and 30 November 1839)

caveats: Editorial date is inferred from book distribution, not physical receipt.
Footnote is editorial evidence, not Darwin body attribution.

dispositions.reason: 535 establishes that Allan had Darwin's letter and was expected to answer; 629A later routes Coral reefs to Allan. Footnote 7 names 535 with 548 as the Malcolmson route for Allan information. The Darwin body does not attribute the information to Malcolmson.
dispositions.response_scope: DCP-LETT-629A body paragraph 4 only; date bounds the documented presentation-copy route.

evidence.quote: Dr Allan has got your last letter
more of this when he answers your questions in detail
The copy for Dr Allan of Forres in Scotland might be sent to Edinburgh & then forwarded
via John Grant Malcolmson (see Correspondence vol. 2, letters from J. G. Malcolmson, 7 October 1839 and 30 November 1839)

caveats: 535 does not say Allan supplied data to Darwin; it says Allan had Darwin's letter and was expected to answer.
This is not a direct reply pair and does not establish earlier receipt.

dispositions.reason: 1147 contains distinctive Glen Roy and parallel-road discussion and predates 558F. Darwin's postscript says he received several private communications, while footnote 9 gives Malcolmson's 2 January letter as an example. The body does not quote Stables, Loch Carron or Dingwall.
dispositions.response_scope: DCP-LETT-558F body paragraph 8 only; no claim that the whole letter responds to 1147.

evidence.quote: the conversation turned on your theory
single lines almost 60 feet broad
I have received several private communications on the subject.
See, for example, Correspondence vol. 1, letter from J. G. Malcolmson, 2 January 1840.

caveats: Generic plural and editorial footnote do not prove that 1147 was one of the communications.
1147 is an incoming reply to Darwin and cannot supply Darwin voice.

dispositions.reason: Keeling overlap is generic: 528 points to a published memoir, while 552 describes Darwin's own Maldeeve and Chagos specimens as islands like Keeling Island. No Malcolmson attribution or distinctive shared detail.

evidence.quote: memoir on the Keeling islands
islands precisely like Keeling Island

caveats: Darwin had independent Beagle and Indian Ocean material.

dispositions.reason: Both discuss glaciers, boulders and the Jura, but 595 contains broad Darwin reasoning with Lyell and no Fifeshire grooved-sandstone detail or Malcolmson attribution. 559's date and assumed Journal receipt cannot establish Darwin receipt.

evidence.quote: grooved and polished surfaces exactly like the limestone of Neuchatel
the Jura blocks

Dr Allan's promised detailed answer and Hardie's Macclesfield Bank notes are information/enclosure routes, not separate Darwin-authored letters in the searched corpus.

issues: No surviving Darwin letter to Malcolmson was located in all_letters.jsonl; no direct incoming-to-Darwin response pair is established.

DCP-LETT-629A paragraph 4 plus footnote 7 is the strongest cross-correspondent evidence. It supports candidate provenance for 535 and 548 by the 17 May 1842 distribution instruction, not an actual first-receipt date.
DCP-LETT-558F paragraph 8 and footnote 9 make 1147 plausible but unproven as one of Darwin's private communications.
General coral, Keeling, Glen Roy, boulder and glacier overlap was rejected where no explicit attribution or distinctive content survived.
Third-party reports, specimens, enclosures and conversations in 535, 548 and 1147 do not become Darwin voice or prove receipt of underlying third-party material at the incoming composition date.
